body_text:
Let $V$ and $W$ be finite-dimensional vector spaces with ordered bases
$\mathcal{B} = \{v_1, \dots, v_n\}$ and $\mathcal{C} = \{w_1, \dots, w_m\}$.
The coordinate representation mapping:
$$ \mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{B}}^{\mathcal{C}} : \mathcal{L}(V, W) \longrightarrow M_{m \times n}(F), \quad T \longmapsto [T]_{\mathcal{B}}^{\mathcal{C}} $$
is an isomorphism of vector spaces.

Furthermore, if $U$ is a third space with basis $\mathcal{D}$ and $S \in \mathcal{L}(W, U)$,
then the matrix of the composite transformation satisfies:
$$ [S \circ T]_{\mathcal{B}}^{\mathcal{D}} = [S]_{\mathcal{C}}^{\mathcal{D}} \cdot [T]_{\mathcal{B}}^{\mathcal{C}}. $$
The classical row-by-column matrix multiplication rule $(AB)_{i,j} = \sum_k A_{i,k} B_{k,j}$
is not an arbitrary convention; it is the unique algebraic formula forced
by the composition of linear maps.
